fields.title: Bye PCOS, Hello PMOS: Why the Common Hormonal Condition Got a New Name
fields.short_description: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is officially being renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS). Discover why medical experts made the change, what PMOS stands for, and how removing the focus from "cysts" will lead to faster diagnoses and better patient care.
fields.blog_body:
Condition Got a New Name
If you or someone you know lives with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, you’ve likely encountered a major source of confusion: you don't actually need ovarian cysts to have PCOS.

Recognizing that the old term led to frequent misdiagnoses and delays in care, global health organizations and medical experts officially renamed the condition to Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS).

Here is what you need to know about the shift and why it matters.

What Does PMOS Stand For?
The new acronym breaks down the actual underlying biology of the condition:

Polyendocrine: Indicates that multiple hormone systems throughout the body are involved (such as elevated androgens and insulin signaling issues), not just reproductive hormones.

Metabolic: Highlights the strong connection to metabolic health, including insulin resistance, blood sugar regulation, and cardiometabolic risks.

Ovarian: Acknowledges the impact on reproductive health and ovulation without overemphasizing physical cysts.

Why Was the Name Changed?
Ovarian Cysts Were Misleading: The "cysts" seen on ultrasounds are actually immature, undeveloped egg follicles—not true fluid-filled cysts. Previously, many patients were told they couldn't have PCOS simply because an ultrasound showed no cysts.

It's More Than a Gynecological Issue: Calling it an "ovary syndrome" framed it strictly as a fertility or reproductive problem. In reality, PMOS is a systemic hormonal and metabolic condition that affects energy, skin, hair, weight, and long-term metabolic health.

Faster Diagnoses: By dropping the focus on cysts, doctors can diagnose and begin supporting patients earlier based on hormonal and metabolic markers.

What Changes for Patients?
While the name is changing, diagnostic criteria and management strategies remain grounded in holistic hormonal care. The transition to PMOS helps ensure that healthcare providers approach treatment with a focus on metabolic balance, lifestyle support, and comprehensive hormone management—rather than just waiting to see cysts on an ultrasound.

fields.title: Web-Slinger Style: Zendaya’s Best Method-Dressing Moments for ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’
fields.short_description: From vintage 1990 Armani spiderweb gowns to $35 graphic tees worn as couture, Zendaya and Law Roach have done it again. Explore the standout method-dressing looks from the Spider-Man: Brand New Day press tour and how they stole the red carpet.
fields.blog_body:
When it comes to movie press tours, no one understands the art of thematic dressing quite like Zendaya and her longtime image architect, Law Roach.

For the global premiere tour of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, the duo took "method dressing" to superhero heights. Weaving spiderweb motifs, archival couture, and deep-cut Marvel references across every stop—from Madrid to Mexico City—here are the standout fashion moments that took over our feeds.

1. The Vintage Armani Spiderweb Dress (London Premiere)
Perhaps her most breathtaking nod to the franchise, Zendaya stepped out in a sheer black floor-length gown from Giorgio Armani’s Spring 1990 collection. Covered in glitzy spiderweb beadwork and intricate brown beaded arachnids across the bodice, the piece was a direct thematic cousin to her iconic Valentino web dress from five years ago.

The Details: Styled with silver crystal-coated Louboutin heels and diamond studs, letting the intricate archival beadwork take center stage.

2. High-Fashion Streetwear in Paris
Proving that method dressing doesn't always require a gown, Zendaya shocked fans in Paris by wearing an oversized vintage black Spider-Man graphic T-shirt as a mini dress.

The Twist: Paired with crisp white pointed-toe pumps, a gold Rolex, and statement earrings, she turned a low-key graphic tee into an effortlessly cool, high-fashion moment alongside Tom Holland's sharp burgundy suit.

3. Archival Galliano & Celestial Webs (London)
In London, her arachnid obsession took a whimsical, astrological turn in an archival 1997 John Galliano "Circus" collection dress. While the front featured a dark blue cloud and zodiac print, the back revealed a literal spiderweb constructed from delicate silver chains strung with charm motifs.

4. Gothic Glamour in Mexico City
Closing out the tour in Mexico City, Zendaya leaned fully into dark romanticism in a dramatic Ashi Studio Couture black lace gown. Featuring a sheer lace overlay, an exaggerated silhouette, and styled with baby bangs and a bouffant, it proved that dark, moody textures can be just as impactful as literal web patterns.

The Verdict
Zendaya and Law Roach continue to set the gold standard for press tour style. By blending high-end archival fashion with clever storytelling, they've turned the Spider-Man: Brand New Day red carpet into a masterclass in fashion history and blockbuster promo.

fields.title: Why NEPSE is Stuck: Understanding Nepal's Sluggish Stock Market
fields.short_description: Hovering in the 2,700s and struggling to sustain a rally, the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) remains stuck in a sideways trend. Discover the key reasons keeping NEPSE stagnant—from tax hikes and tight liquidity to investor fatigue—and what needs to change.
fields.blog_body:
Investors hoping for a massive bull run on the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) have mostly been met with sideways movement and sudden pullbacks. Despite brief spikes after political shifts or policy announcements, the market continues to bounce around the 2,700–2,750 point range rather than making a sustained climb toward past all-time highs.

If you’re wondering why your portfolio isn't moving, here are the core factors holding NEPSE back.

1. Increased Capital Gains Tax & Budget Uncertainty
The government's budget introduced higher capital gains taxes on share transactions—raising short-term rates to 10% (up from 7.5%) and long-term rates to 7.5% (up from 5%).

The Impact: Higher transaction costs immediately squeezed profit margins for short-term traders. Combined with initial confusion around whether gains would face additional taxation for high earners, institutional and retail investors quickly adopted a "wait-and-see" approach.

2. Profit-Booking at Resistance Levels
Every time the index inches toward 2,800 or 2,900 points, heavy sell-offs trigger almost immediately. Many investors who bought at higher levels over the past two years are eager to exit at breakeven, creating a strong ceiling (resistance) that absorbs buyer momentum before a rally can build steam.

3. Tight Liquidity and Bank Cautiousness
While interest rates have eased compared to peak levels, banks and financial institutions remain conservative with margin lending.

Where's the Volume? Without aggressive institutional buying or easy access to low-cost leverage, daily turnover drops. A healthy bull market needs persistent, high turnover to sustain a rise—something NEPSE currently lacks on a daily basis.

4. Oversupply of Shares (The IPO Boom)
The rapid influx of new initial public offerings (IPOs), rights shares, and secondary offerings—particularly in the hydropower sector—has significantly diluted market capital. With more shares floating around the market than there is fresh cash to absorb them, individual stock prices struggle to rise sharply.

What Will It Take to Turn the Tide?
For NEPSE to break out of this cycle, the market needs a combination of:

Policy Clarity: Clear tax guidelines and pro-investor regulatory steps from NRB and SEBON.

Fresh Institutional Capital: Increased participation from mutual funds, corporate investors, and long-term buyers.

Sustained Turnover: Consistent daily trading volumes staying above NRs 8–10 billion to signal genuine market confidence.

fields.title: Spicing Up the Streets: Why Nepali Youth Are Obsessed with Laphing & Tibetan Food
fields.short_description: How did a cold Tibetan street food conquer Kathmandu's food scene? From the alleyways of Boudha to every college corner, discover why Nepali youth are obsessed with Laphing and Tibetan comfort food.
fields.blog_body:
If you walk through the vibrant alleys of Boudha, Swayambhu, or near any college campus in the Kathmandu Valley, you’ll hear a familiar sound: the rapid clack-clack of knives slicing cold jelly noodles on wooden chopping boards.

While momo will always hold the crown for Nepal's ultimate comfort food, a new champion has dominated the youth food scene in recent years: Laphing (and the broader lineup of Tibetan street snacks).

Here is why this cold, fire-spiced dish went from a hyper-local neighborhood secret to a national craze among young Nepalis.

1. The Ultimate Flavor Profile: Cold, Tangy & Fiery
Unlike traditional Nepali street snacks that are served piping hot (like samosas or chow mein), Laphing is served cold. Made from potato, wheat, or mung bean starch, the slippery, jelly-like noodles themselves are neutral in taste—acting as a blank canvas for an explosion of flavors:

Sichuan chili oil for a fiery kick

Garlic water & vinegar for sharp sourness

Sesame oil & soy sauce for a savory umami finish

This contrast between ice-cold jelly and burning spice creates an addictive sensory hit that keeps students and young adults coming back for more.

2. The Fusion Upgrade: Wai Wai & Crunch
Part of Laphing's massive surge in popularity comes from local adaptation. Innovative shopkeepers began customizing traditional Tibetan rolls to cater to Nepali palates:

Dry Laphing with Wai Wai: Crushed instant noodles stuffed inside the roll add a signature crunch.

Chips & Peanuts: Lay's potato chips or roasted peanuts added for extra texture.

Soup vs. Dry Options: Giving eaters control over how drowned in chili-vinegar broth they want their plate to be.

3. Extremely Budget-Friendly
For high school and college students hanging out after class, affordability is everything. At around NRs 50 to 100 per plate, Laphing offers a quick, filling, and intensely flavorful snack that fits comfortably into any student's daily allowance.

4. The "Boudha Vibe" & Social Media Magnet
Food is as much about the experience as the taste. Hanging out in Boudha or Swayambhu, enjoying a plate of Laphing on plastic stools while listening to ambient Tibetan mantras or catching up with friends, became a social ritual.

Add colorful yellow and white rolls, red chili oil, and aesthetic street-food plating to the mix, and Laphing became instant fuel for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube shorts, spreading the trend rapidly beyond Kathmandu to Pokhara, Chitwan, and Dharan.

The Takeaway
The rise of Laphing is a testament to how culinary cultures naturally blend and evolve. What started as a humble dish brought by Tibetan communities has become an undeniable staple of modern Nepali youth culture—one spicy, slippery bite at a time.

fields.title: Beyond the Crowds: Why Dhorpatan is Nepal’s Best-Kept Travel Secret
fields.short_description: Escape the crowded trails of Annapurna and Everest for Dhorpatan—Nepal’s only hunting reserve. Discover vast high-altitude meadows, blue sheep grazing against Dhaulagiri views, and authentic western mountain culture.
fields.blog_body:
If you ask most travelers to picture trekking in Nepal, they think of steep staircases on the Annapurna Circuit or dense crowds marching toward Everest Base Camp.

So when you step into Dhorpatan, the sheer geography hits you first: a vast, flat-bottomed alpine valley stretching as far as the eye can see, framed by dense rhododendron forests and the towering peaks of Dhaulagiri and Gurja Himal.

Spread across Baglung, Myagdi, and Rukum, Dhorpatan remains one of the most untouched, tranquil, and unique high-altitude destinations in western Nepal. Here is why it deserves a spot on your off-the-beaten-path bucket list.

1. Nepal’s Only Hunting Reserve
Established in 1987, Dhorpatan holds a singular status as the country’s only official hunting reserve. Before you worry—no, it is not an open shooting range.

Controlled, highly regulated seasonal hunting permits are auctioned exclusively for specific non-endangered animals—primarily Blue Sheep (Bharal) and Himalayan Tahr—to maintain balanced wildlife populations and fund local community conservation. For regular travelers and trekkers, it functions just like a serene, protected national park where you can spot rare wildlife roaming freely.

2. A Landscape Unlike Anywhere Else in Nepal
Most mountain routes in Nepal cut through narrow, dramatic river gorges. Dhorpatan is completely different:

Vast Patans (Meadows): Flat, golden-green grasslands sit at an altitude of ~2,850 meters, perfect for easy walking and wild camping.

Horse Herds & Timber Houses: Horses graze freely across the plateau, while traditional wooden and stone houses give the valley a timeless, western frontier feel.

Endless Wildlife: Beyond blue sheep, the reserve is home to red pandas, musk deer, Himalayan black bears, and over 130 bird species (including Nepal’s national bird, the Lophophorus).

3. Untouched Local Culture
Unlike commercialized trek stops where every second house is a modern lodge with Wi-Fi, Dhorpatan offers genuine local hospitality.

The valley is home to a mix of Kham Magar communities and seasonal migratory herders who move up to the high pastures during the warmer months. Staying in local homesteads or tea houses gives you a rare look into traditional mountain life, indigenous dialects, and authentic local food.

How to Get There & When to Go
Getting There: The typical route goes from Pokhara → Baglung → Burtibang by road, followed by a scenic drive or trek up into Dhorpatan Valley.

Best Time to Visit:

Spring (March–May): Rhododendron forests burst into pink and red, and temperatures are pleasant.

Autumn (September–November): Crystal-clear skies offer incredible views of the Dhaulagiri range.

The Takeaway
If you crave wide-open space, silence, and a side of the Himalayas that fewer than a thousand travelers get to see each year, Dhorpatan is waiting. Pack a good pair of boots, leave the crowd behind, and take in one of Nepal's true hidden gems.

fields.title: "She's Got Balls": Why Even Our Compliments to Women Are Misogynistic
fields.short_description: "She's got balls of steel." We say it as a compliment, but why do we use male anatomy to describe a woman’s bravery? Explore how backhanded compliments reveal deeply ingrained gender bias—and how to fix our language.
fields.blog_body:
When a woman does something exceptionally brave—whether standing up to a powerful executive, speaking truth to authority, or making a high-stakes gamble—the phrase you'll inevitably hear is:

"She’s got real balls." or "She has balls of steel."

It’s intended as high praise. But if you pause to think about it, the irony is glaring: To compliment a woman’s strength, we attribute it to an organ she doesn't even have.

The Problem With "Male-Coded" Strength
Phrases like "balls of steel" sound empowering on the surface, but they quietly reinforce a frustrating double standard:

Strength is Treated as Inherent to Men: It implies that true courage, grit, and authority are fundamentally male traits. For a woman to be brave, society acts as though she has to "borrow" male anatomy to pull it off.

Female Resilience Gets Erased: Women endure incredible physical, mental, and emotional challenges every day—from childbirth to navigating systemic inequality. Yet, when describing peak human courage, our default slang acts as if endurance belongs exclusively to men.

Men Remain the Default: Just like "man up" frames weakness as acting like a girl, "she’s got balls" frames strength as acting like a man. Both sides of the coin keep men as the standard for human capability and women as the exception.

Better Ways to Describe Real Courage
Women don't need male-coded metaphors to be recognized for their strength. English is packed with powerful, non-gendered words that hit much harder:

Instead of: "She’s got balls of steel."

Try:

"She has an iron spine."

"She’s completely fearless."

"She has unmatched nerve."

"She’s an absolute powerhouse."

The Takeaway
A woman standing firm in the face of fear or pressure isn't "acting like a man"—she is simply demonstrating human courage. If we want a culture that truly respects women, we need to stop treating female bravery like a male trait.
